gx_front_1#1.killer: gold particles caught per 1-m sample by a 2-cm hole in placer pay gravel (bankable assay statistics)
gx_front_1#1.why: A finger-thin hole catches about one gold flake per metre even in a rich Kolyma placer, against ~20 needed for a +/-50% assay, so it cannot give bankable grade, and exploration is only ~6% of delivered cost anyway.

EC:EB:g1_loop#2.killer: share of Laptev-launched floes that reach Fram Strait
EC:EB:g1_loop#2.why: Even with chosen launch points at most half of Laptev ice ever joined the Transpolar Drift (about a fifth survives today), and bags, two years of 14% money and a token pickup already cost as much as the rail freight they replace.

EC:EB:g2_evo2#1.killer: near-bed wave orbital velocity needed to stir 0.5-mm sand in a 1-m-deep pond
EC:EB:g2_evo2#1.why: Waves on a pond this small are too short to reach the floor: even a gale stirs it at ~2 cm/s, a quarter of what 0.5-mm sand needs and ~5% of what 20-mm stones need, so the sorting that would halve placer cost never starts.

g1_mech#3.killer: yearly release volume to float 1.4 Mt of concentrate 100 km down a 20-m creek at 0.8 m depth
g1_mech#3.why: The barges fall behind the crest, so the release must run for the whole voyage, and one small-creek snowmelt carries under a quarter of a Baimskaya-size year while a free creek route would trim only the 5% outbound share.

erp2_a#3.killer: charge per kg of grain needed for the claimed 41-cm drift at 300 kV/m over a 1.5-m fall
erp2_a#3.why: Measured charging of the feldspar and quartz waste gives about half the claimed drift, and even the idea's own saving is under 3% of delivered lithium carbonate cost.

gx_fl_1#2.killer: hoop strap tension at the base of a 60-m tailings thickener holding 6 m of slurry, safety factor 4
gx_fl_1#2.why: The "a sixth of burst" check compares pressure, but strap tension grows with tank radius, so a 60-m thickener wall needs about 4x the hoop strength ever demonstrated, and the shells reach at most a quarter of capex.

g1_core2#2.killer: barrel life at ~1.5 km/s with 100-500 kg rounds
g1_core2#2.why: A gun this fast wears out its barrel in about 65 rounds against ~12,800 a day needed for Baimskaya, and the launch energy alone costs more than the whole outbound logistics bill.

gx_ledg_1#2.killer: seam area gasified per well pair
gx_ledg_1#2.why: Underground gasification itself is proven, but a well pair sweeps about 0.2 ha rather than the 1.5 ha assumed, and at 10 kt/yr the station's crew, plant and 2-3 new well pairs a year cost more than the barge and winter-road chain they remove.

EC:EB:g2_imm#3.killer: winter electricity from freezing the leach liquor vs electrowinning demand, per kg Cu (2 g/L PLS frozen 96% to reach CuSO4 saturation; Nov–Mar air −31 °C; 5 K/10 K heat-exchanger approaches; 0.6 of Carnot)
EC:EB:g2_imm#3.why: Freezing covers only ~60% of the electrowinning power (100% only if the whole season averaged −40 °C), and SX plus diesel are too small a share of cost to pay for a plant that must freeze ~480 t of liquor per tonne of copper.

EC:EB:g1_genius#3.killer: ice that must leave the sand before the dry electrostatic roll vs the "free drying" of −30 °C air
EC:EB:g1_genius#3.why: Frozen ground is not dry ground: the pore ice stays on the grains, and removing it with −30 °C air would take ~1.2×10^5 m³ of air per tonne of sand, so the gold never reaches the roll as free grains.

EC:EB:g2_evo1#3.killer: winter sublimation flux from the gravel pad
EC:EB:g2_evo1#3.why: The measured sublimation is about 1/3 of what is needed, so the pad would have to be ~3.3 km²; snowfall (~0.4 mm/day, ~5× the sublimation) buries it anyway, and the extra handling makes each ounce dearer.

g1_core2#1.killer: rate at which ponded, darkened yedoma deepens by thaw
g1_core2#1.why: A 1.5 m channel would take ~24 years to form (while the banks retreat ~1.2 m/yr), and even a finished canal only shortens one leg of the delivery chain.

EC:EB:g2_evo1#2.killer: under-ice river discharge needed to carry a season's sand (100,000 m³ of 1 mm sand over 120 days at 1.5 m/s under the keel; Meyer-Peter–Müller bedload formula)
EC:EB:g2_evo1#2.why: Placer rivers carry about 1/20 of the winter flow needed (most freeze through, or overflow as aufeis when the keel chokes them), and even a working version saves only the washing, ~8% of the chain.

g1_core2#3.killer: average amount the film surface must stay below air temperature over the thaw season to keep the thaw inside a 2 m gravel pad (Stefan formula: at most 541 °C·day of surface thawing)
g1_core2#3.why: The film supplies only ~60% of the cooling needed in the Arctic (~25% in central Yakutia), cannot be laid on driven-over or dusty surfaces, and foundations are too small a share of delivered cost for the chain to change.

gx_front_2#2.killer: ammonia made per tonne of ore ground vs ammonia the leach consumes (sulphide sulphur ends up as ammonium sulphate; ore with 1% Ni + 1% Cu)
gx_front_2#2.why: Even at the lab-record efficiency the mill makes about 1/1,000 of the ammonia the leach consumes, and if it did make it all, the electrolytic hydrogen alone ($746/t) would cost about three times the inbound logistics it removes ($255/t).

g1_mech#2.killer: reduction in hauled tonnage that dry electrostatic sorting achieves at usable recovery
g1_mech#2.why: Dry charge sorting achieves about half the required tonnage cut at worse recovery than the dense-media and flotation plants already concentrating on site, so the hauled tonnage does not fall and delivered cost rises.
